question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), can more than one child of the same parent /Guardian avail scholarship under the scheme?
answer: Not more than one child of the same parents/guardians will be eligible and to certify this a self-certification will be required from the candidate. An individual can be given the award only once and cannot be considered for the award for second or subsequent time.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is the time period within which candidate need to join the course after obtaining provisional award letter?
answer: A selected candidate is required to join within 2 year of receipt of intimation from this Ministry regarding selection for the award/assurance. On expiry of this specified period of time, the award automatically gets cancelled.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), which documents have to be uploaded on the Ministry portal?
answer: The students are required to upload either the copy of award of degree (M.Phil./Ph.D) or course completion certificate. In addition to this, thesis report also has to be uploaded at tribal repository.

question: Who are eligible to apply for National Fellowship Scholarship Schemes?
answer: The candidates belonging to Scheduled Tribes (ST) who have passed the Post-Graduation examination and fulfilling the Scheme guidelines of Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) are eligible to apply for these fellowship

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), can I avail any other scholarship from Central/ State Government for the same study?
answer: The ST students once considered eligible for the Fellowship shall not be entitled for any other scholarship of the Central or State Government the same study. If selected, candidate should refund the money to concerned agency for the selected year.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), how can a Student upgrade course from M.Phil to Ph.D?
answer: The Student’s is required to submit upgradation certificate issued by the Committee of three members comprising of Head of the Department, Supervisor and one outside subject expert to be constituted by the concerned Department of the University/Institution/College for evaluation of the work of student.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what should be the Type and size of the documents and profile photo to be uploaded?
answer: All documents should be uploaded in pdf file and the Profile Photo should be in.jpg/.jpeg format (Size: - 50 KB-100KB).

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what should I do, if I do not find my university name in the dropdown menu?
answer: You can select “other option” from the drop-down list and type your university/Institute name in the specified box.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), is there any Award No?
answer: A provisional award number will be provided to the candidate on the basis of Domicile state mentioned in application Form. Once his/her application is submitted online, students should remember their ID till the course completion if selected. All communication with the Ministry will be made by using this ID.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), how should I check the status of my application online?
answer: After login, enter valid Award no and Password to check the status. Your application status shows as “Pending” or “submitted” under the option ‘Check Your Status’.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what are the criteria for selection?
answer: The selection of the students takes place on the based on the marks obtained in Post Graduation Course.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), how do I know the name and address of the Nodal Officer?
answer: The name and contact details of the Nodal Officer are available with university/Institute who is dealing with NFST.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), which documents have to be sent to the Ministry after the selection?
answer: The students are required to send the following documents to the Ministry after selection:  Original bond paper duly filled (Execute on non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 50 or above/e-stamp paper)

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), which documents have to be submitted to the University after the selection?
answer: The Student is required to submit the documents to as and when asked by the university.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), when does students have to update a Research Topic?
answer: The students are required to update research details at portal in the Research section after joining the Course.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), when does students has to submit a progress report?
answer: The students are required to submit the progress report to the university on yearly basis.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what should students do if the joining date is wrongly mentioned in the joining report?
answer: The students are required to re-submit the joining report to the University with actual date of joining. University is required to modify joining date while linking the ID at Canara Bank portal

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), is It necessary to upload all the documents (Continuation certificate/HRA Certificate etc.) for continuous fellowship?
answer: The student’s is required to upload all the documents (continuation certificate/HRA Certificate etc.) for availing fellowship on portal. Without uploading aforesaid documents fellowship will not be processed by the ministry.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what should students do if the account status is shown as “Student ID Withheld”?
answer: The student may request to the nodal officer of the University to initiate “withheld removal “option and get the approval from the Ministry.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is the meaning of “Initiation awaited from University” with respect to uploading documents?
answer: “Initiation awaited from University” means approval is pending from the University.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), do the students have to refund the Scholarship amount if the same has been availed from other sources?
answer: Yes, the student is required to refund the amount of Scholarship/fellowship availed from other sources. Otherwise, fellowship will not be processed, if student does not refund the availed amount to concern university/State/other agency.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is the “No Objection Certificate” (NoC) and where does it have to be uploaded?
answer: The students who have not availed any scholarship/fellowship from any other source are required to submit “No Objection Certificate” athttps://tribal.nic.in/Grievance/ under the section “NOC/Refund receipt”

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), which documents student is required to submit to the University, after completion of the course?
answer: The students are required to submit either the copy of award of degree (M.Phil./Ph.D) or course completion certificate to the university. The details of course completion need to be filled by the University on the ministry portal, failing which the payment for the last 3 months will not be released.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), how beneficiary code will be generated, if “Beneficiary code rejected, as shown in Canara bank portal?
answer: The beneficiary code will be rejected if IFSC code wrongly entered/ account closed/blocked. The University is required to update valid account no with IFSC code in the portal and get approved by the ministry.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is mode of Payment of Fellowship?
answer: Payment of fellowship to the selected students will be made on quarterly basis, through the Direct Benefit Transfer system by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the accredited bank after approval from the Ministry.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), can I change my bank account details if mentioned/mismatched in university record/Canara Bank Portal? wrongly
answer: The request letter from University/Institute along with photo copy of passbook should sent to Ministry, after approval from competent authority, the account no may be changed in coordination with Bank by the University.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is the last date for linking of student’s id at Canara Bank Portal?
answer: There is no such last date for linking of student’s id at canara bank portal. The students are required to link their id on time for the process of fellowship amount. Delay in linking, delay in payment process.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what should I do if canara bank show payment generated but the amount has not been credited in my account?
answer: Payment file generation by Canara Bank through PFMS is initial stage after uploading your documents at Canara Bank portal. There are series of procedure/stages followed at different level for releasing the amount to the students.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), what is the procedure for claiming contingency?
answer: The students are required to submit actual bill of expenditure incurred by him/her to the university on quarterly basis. University will verify your bill and they will enter online at the portal.

question: Under the National Fellowship for ST students (NFST), if a student has completed his/her course before or after 5 years, for how long will he /she will get the scholarship?
answer: Total duration for availing fellowship is 2 years for M.Phil, 5 years fro Ph.D, 5 years for integrated M.Phil+Ph.D. Beyond that, the Ministry will not allow to the students to avail fellowship. In case a student has completed his/her course before the duration, he/she will get the fellowship till the final submission of thesis.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), is 55 % marks compulsory for those candidates who have already taken admission in Institutes abroad?
answer: The criteria of marks obtained in Bachelor’s/Master’s Degree will not apply to those candidates who have already obtained admission in top 1,000 Institutes as QS world ranking of the latest available report.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), who can issue the income certificate?
answer: The Income certificate should be issued by competent authority/designated officer (i.e. Tehsildar/Deputy Commissioner/ Executive Magistrate/etc.) of State Government.

question: If applicant has already joined university and selected for NOS, from which date applicant will receive scholarship.
answer: Applicant will receive proportionate scholarship from date of issuing provisional award letter.

question: Who can apply for National Overseas Scholarship Scheme?
answer: ST students fulfilling eligibility criteria of the scheme and wishing to pursue higher studies abroad for Masters and PhD programmes in top 1000 QS World Ranking Universities/Institutions. The guidelines for eligibility criteria and other details may be seen at https://overseas.tribal.gov.in/.

question: How many slots/awards available for National Overseas Scholarship?
answer: There are 20 slots/awards per year (Number of slots/awards may vary) are available for National Overseas Scholarship.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), who are the family members included for income criteria?
answer: The combined income of father and mother is considered as family income if both are working. In case of only one parent is alive, the income of that parent shall be taken into account for considering total family income.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), what should be submitted if the father is alive but his income is Zero or his income details have not been reported in the application?
answer: If the father is alive but his income is zero or his income has not been reported, the applicant must submit a declaration in the prescribed format (available on portal) clearly stating the reason for non-reporting of the father's income. The application may be considered incomplete without this declaration.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), what document is required if the applicant's father is deceased?
answer: If the applicant's father is deceased, the father's death certificate must be submitted as supporting document along with the application.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), what should student do, in case of any problem while filling the application form in Google Chrome?
answer: If students face any problem while filling the application form in Google Chrome, it is advised to use internet explorer. In case of any issue/error in internet explorer as well, it is advised to clear browser history /cache and try again.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), can I edit the information after final submission?
answer: No, application cannot be edited after final submission. Applicant can edit information before final submission. However, before submission all saved information can be edited except “Registration Details”.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), do I have to fill up the online application in one sitting?
answer: No, you can fill up the online application in as many sittings by clicking ‘Save Draft’ button, until you are satisfied that you have entered all desirable fields correctly. The software provides auto save facility to save your application at every stage until you click on ‘Submit’ button finally.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), what should I do if I forget my password?
answer: The process of re-set of the password is given as below: Student login->Forgot Password Enter the registered mobile number and click on the submit button. Enter OTP received on registered mobile Number and enter new password, Click the submit button.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), what is difference between provisionally award letter and confirmation award letter?
answer: A provisional award letter is issued immediately after the declaration of results, whereas the confirmation letter is provided only after the verification of specific documents by the concerned authorities and the submission of all required documents necessary for joining the institution abroad.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), who will arrange the Air ticket to proceed abroad for joining the university or institute?
answer: Student has to submit/upload the ticket booking request in prescribed format at Ministry portal & send email before one month of departure. Accordingly, Ministry will arrange the Air ticket.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), can I get tuition fee and Visa fee in advance from Ministry?
answer: No, Ministry will not provide any payment in advance. After joining the course in the university, the University will send bills/vouchers to the respective Indian Mission. Indian Mission will release the payment and claim from the Ministry on reimbursement basis.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), if I extend the course beyond course duration, what is the procedure?
answer: Course Extension beyond the prescribed duration is allowed only on the recommendation of the University, but without any kind of financial assistance except return air ticket to India.

question: If I am selected for a State Government scholarship and also selected under the NOS (Central Government) scheme, can I avail both scholarships?
answer: No, you can avail only one scholarship—either from the State Government or the Central Government.

question: Under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), if there is a spelling mistake in the community’s name of the uploaded ST certificate, will it be accepted?
answer: No. The community’s name must exactly match with the latest Gazette notification.

question: What is the Prime Minister’s Scholarship Scheme (PMSS)?
answer: PMSS is a scholarship scheme launched under the National Defence Fund to encourage technical and professional education for the wards and widows of personnel of CAPFs, Assam Rifles, and States/UTs Police personnel martyred in Terror/Naxal attacks.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what is the minimum educational qualification required?
answer: New Applicants: Must have secured at least 60% in the Minimum Entry Qualification (MEQ) such as 10+2, diploma or graduation. - Renewal Applicants: Must pass each academic year with at least 50% marks.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what is the duration and amount of the scholarship?
answer: Duration: Up to 5 years (based on course duration). - Amount: ₹3,000/month for girls and ₹2,500/month for boys (paid annually).

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), is there a quota for scholarships?
answer: Yes. Each year under fresh category: - 2,000 scholarships (1,000 for boys and 1,000 for girls) for CAPFs & AR categories. - 500 scholarships (250 for boys and 250 for girls) for States/UTs Police category. Note: Quotas are not interchangeable between genders.

question: What courses are covered under PMSS?
answer: Only the first professional degree courses such as BE, B.Tech, MBBS, BDS, BBA, BCA, B.Pharma, B.Sc Nursing etc., recognized by AICTE, UGC, MCI etc. are eligible. Refer to Appendix-I in the guidelines for the full list.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), are integrated courses eligible?
answer: Yes, but only the professional component of an integrated course is eligible. For dual professional degrees, only the first professional component is covered.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what is the selection criteria for fresh applications?
answer: Selection is based on: 1. Category preference. 2. Percentage in MEQ. 3. Age (higher age preferred). 4. Parent's rank (lower rank preferred).

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), can students studying abroad or in unrecognized colleges apply?
answer: No. PMSS is not applicable to students studying abroad or enrolled in institutions not recognized by UGC, AICTE, MCI, or other regulatory bodies.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what happens if I submit incorrect or false information?
answer: Such applications will be rejected and the scholarship will be cancelled and required to refund the scholarship amount with interest.

question: Can I apply for PMSS if I am already in the second year of a course?
answer: Yes, if you were admitted directly to the 2nd year via lateral entry (e.g., after diploma in engineering), you are eligible. But PMSS is not applicable for second-year admission through regular progression.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), is there any age limit to apply for the scholarship?
answer: There is no specific age limit mentioned, but preference is given to applicants of higher age during merit-based selection.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), can I apply again next year if I missed applying this year?
answer: Yes, but only if you are still in your first year and fulfill all eligibility criteria. For renewal, a grace period of one year is allowed in case of delay in applying.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what happens if my application is rejected or marked as defective?
answer: If your application is rejected or marked defective due to any issue, you must correct and resubmit it before the verification deadline. If the application is withdrawn, you may reapply within the open window of NSP.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), when will the scholarship amount be credited to my account?
answer: After final verification and merit selection, the amount will be directly credited into your Aadhaar-seeded bank account through PFMS, typically within a few weeks of final processing.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), can I edit my application after submission?
answer: Once submitted, no changes can be made. However, withdrawal and re-application is allowed before Level-2 (Force Nodal Officer) verification, using the standard withdrawal reasons provided as drop-down menu.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), will I receive any official communication upon selection?
answer: Yes. Once you select for the scholarship, a system generated confirmation through text massage will be received on registered mobile number.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), what is the role of the college/institute in my application?
answer: Your college/institute must verify your application and uploaded documents online. Unverified applications will not be processed for selection.

question: Under the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS), can students from private colleges apply?
answer: Yes, provided the college/institute is approved by UGC/AICTE/MCI or the relevant government regulatory authority. The course listed in Appendix-I of the guidelines.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what is the objective of the Scheme?
answer: The Scheme aims to provide quality coaching to economically disadvantaged Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and beneficiaries of the PM CARES Children Scheme to help them prepare for competitive examinations for employment and admission to reputed professional institutions.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, who is eligible under the Scheme?
answer: The following are eligible: SC students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh. OBC students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh. Beneficiaries of the PM CARES Children Scheme (no income or caste restriction).

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, is there any income limit?
answer: Yes. For SC and OBC candidates, the annual family income from all sources should not exceed ₹8 lakh. This condition does not apply to PM CARES beneficiaries.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, which competitive examinations are covered?
answer: The Scheme covers coaching for: UPSC Civil Services State PSC SSC Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) Banking, Insurance and PSU examinations JEE NEET CAT CLAT GRE GMAT SAT IELTS TOEFL GATE CA-CPT NDA CDS Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) and other approved examinations.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, how many times can a student avail the benefit?
answer: A student can avail the benefit not more than two times, irrespective of the examination or number of attempts.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, is Aadhaar mandatory?
answer: Yes. Students must have an Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account. If Aadhaar is not available at the time of application, the Enrolment ID (EID) may be used, but payment will be released only after Aadhaar is obtained and linked.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what is the minimum academic eligibility?
answer: For coaching after Class XII, students must have secured at least 50% marks in Class X. For coaching after graduation, students must have secured at least 50% marks in Class XII.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, who implements the Scheme?
answer: The Scheme is implemented by the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF) through empanelled Central Universities operating as Dr. Ambedkar Centres of Excellence (DACE).

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what is the SC:OBC ratio?
answer: Seats are allocated in the ratio of 70:30 between SC and OBC students. The percentage of SC students shall not be less than 70%, although DAF may relax this in exceptional cases, subject to a minimum of 50% SC students.

question: Are PM CARES beneficiaries selected through merit?
answer: No. All eligible PM CARES beneficiaries are admitted without the merit selection process and are over and above the normal seat allocation.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what financial assistance is provided?
answer: Eligible students receive: Course fee (as per prescribed ceiling) Monthly stipend of ₹4,000 One-time incentive of ₹15,000 for interview coaching after qualifying the Mains examination of Civil Services.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, how is the scholarship released?
answer: Payments are made through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the Aadhaar-enabled bank account of the student in two instalments.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what is the attendance requirement?
answer: Students must maintain regular attendance. Those absent for more than four days in a month without a valid reason may have their candidature cancelled. Attendance is recorded through Aadhaar-based biometric authentication.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, can coaching begin before payment is received?
answer: Yes. Central Universities are required to allow eligible students to join coaching even if the first instalment has not yet been released.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what happens if false information is submitted?
answer: Submission of false information or forged documents may result in: Cancellation of candidature, Recovery of the amount released, along with 15% compound interest, and Administrative and/or criminal proceedings.

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, what are the maximum coaching fees?
answer: The maximum admissible coaching fee depends on the course. Examples include: UPSC/State PSC: ₹75,000 SSC/RRB: ₹40,000 Banking/CAT/CLAT: ₹50,000 JEE/NEET/GATE: ₹75,000 GRE/GMAT/IELTS/TOEFL: ₹35,000 NDA/CDS: ₹20,000 CPL: ₹30,000

question: Under the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs, OBCs and PM CARES beneficiaries, can a Central University offer additional seats beyond the allocated quota?
answer: Yes. Universities may admit additional students at their own cost, subject to infrastructure availability. No financial assistance will be provided by the Ministry for such students.

question: What is NSPG Scheme?
answer: National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS) is an umbrella scheme by merging four different scholarship schemes for postgraduate studies i.e. (i) PG Indira Gandhi single girl child scholarship, (ii) PG scholarship for university rank holders, (iii) PG scholarship for SC/ST students pursuing professional courses and (iv) Post Graduate Scholarship for GATE/GPAT.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), how can I apply online for scholarship?
answer: Students can apply online through National Scholarship Portal (NSP).

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), does reservation system is followed in this scholarship? If yes what percentage is reserved for each respective category?
answer: Yes. The slots are allocated as per Govt. of India reservation policy. However, 30% slots will be reserved for the women candidates. Preference is given to single girl child.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), what is the definition of Single Girl Child?
answer: A 'Single Girl Child' is defined as the only girl child in the family without any brothers or sisters. If a family has one or more sons and one daughter, the daughter is not considered a single girl child. However, a girl scholar who is one of the twin daughters or fraternal daughters is eligible to apply for the scholarship.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), can Student apply in the PG Scholarship when he has enrolled in Integrated programme?
answer: Yes, the student can apply. In case of integrated programmes, the scholarship shall be given for PG component only.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), how may slots are available in PG Studies?
answer: Ten thousand (10000) slots per annum.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), what is the amount of PG scholarship?
answer: The rate of Rs.15,000/- per month for 10 months in a year.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), how many slots are reserved for women candidates?
answer: 30% slots will be reserved for the women candidates. Preference is given to single girl child.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), can students who are doing PG through distance mode apply for PG studies?
answer: No. This scholarship is for regular mode students only.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), if a student who gets another scholarship can apply for this scheme?
answer: No, the students can avail only one scholarship at a time.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), is it necessary to have AISHE code for university or college?
answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the University/College/Institute to have a valid AISHE code for accessing the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). The institution with AISHE code can get themselves registered on NSP portal through District/State nodal officers for NSP.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), i have submitted the application. Am I eligible to receive the scholarship?
answer: After submission of application, the same is verified first by INO and then the SNO. Thereafter, the merit is prepared. The student is eligible for scholarship only if he/she is selected in the merit list.

question: Under the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS), how to know the contact details of various Nodal Officers?
answer: The Scheme wise details of Nodal Officers is available under the Public Link of the NSP Portal.

question: Which students can apply for renewal in NSPG.
answer: The scholarship are renewed for the next year of study on successful completion of first year of study. The students are required to apply for ‘Renewal’ of their scholarship on the NSP. Scholarship for 2 nd year will not be processed without successful submission of renewal application.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, can all NER students apply for the scholarship?
answer: No, the students with North Eastern domicile are eligible to apply. The income of the parents of the student should be below Rs. 04.50 lakh per annum.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, those students who have completed UG degree and want to do UG again, can they still apply?
answer: Students, who have already acquired any UG degree, are not eligible to apply. The scholarship is available for 1st UG degree only.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, what is the procedure of selection under this scholarship.
answer: 50% of slots are earmarked for Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Law, Management and other 50% are earmarked for Science, Engineering & Technology, medical, technical, agriculture, forestry programmes. The selection is done purely on the basis of state-wise merit from among the candidates who have applied for the scholarship under the scheme.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, how many times applications are invited in a year?
answer: Applications are invited once in a year on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) of the Government of India.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, what is the procedure of scholarship disbursement.
answer: The scholarship amount is disbursed by UGC through DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) Mode and transferred to the Bank account which is seeded with Aadhaar.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, can the application be canceled after verification by the institute?
answer: The application may be canceled if the student or institution provides wrong/misleading information on the portal.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, how to know the deadlines for application submission and verification of application at Institute/District/State Level?
answer: The deadlines for application submission and verification are displayed on NSP.

question: Under the Ishan Uday Scholarship, can students edit the application after closing date?
answer: No, student cannot edit the application after closing date. Incomplete applications will be summarily rejected. Only verified online applications will be considered for award of scholarship.

question: What are the eligibility criteria for applying the “Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students”?
answer: PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students is a merit-cum-means scholarship scheme. Eligibility conditions for FRESH application: Students who are above 80th percentile of successful candidates in the relevant stream from a particular Board of Examination in Class XII Students pursuing regular course (not correspondence or distance mode) Having family income upto Rs. 4.5 lakh per annum Not receiving any other scholarship or fee reimbursement of any kind Diploma students are not eligible under the scheme. Students who had taken a drop after 12th class are not eligible under the scheme.

question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), what is the rate of scholarship under the Scheme?
answer: The rate of scholarship is Rs. 12,000/- per annum at Graduation level for first three years of College and University courses and Rs. 20,000/- per annum at Post-Graduation level. Students pursuing technical courses are paid Rs. 20,000/- per annum in the 4th and 5th year. Students pursing B.Tech/ BE would get scholarship for 4 years only i.e Rs. 12000 per annum for first three years and Rs. 20,000 per annum in the 4 th year.

question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), how a second/ third/ fourth year student gets scholarships?
answer: All the students finally selected for scholarship in first year are eligible for renewal of scholarships in 2nd/ 3rd years subject to fulfilment of certain eligibility conditions. The students have to apply again in the same portal as renewal applicant and provide necessary marksheets, etc. for this. The applicant should not receive scholarship from any other department/ ministry.

question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), what is the duration of scholarships and criteria for renewal under the scheme?
answer: A student will be eligible for the scholarship for a total duration not exceeding 5 years. A scholarship under the scheme is renewable on year-to-year basis up to Post Graduate level (except for the students pursuing technical courses leading to degree at graduation level). Student must secure at least 50% marks and maintain adequate attendance of at least 75%.

question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), what is Aadhaar Seeding with Bank Account?
answer: The Aadhaar Seeding means linking Aadhaar holder’s Unique 12-digit AADHAAR number with their Bank Account number for receiving Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) provided under various Government schemes like, Scholarships.

question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), how to seed an Aadhaar number with a Bank Account?
answer: The following is the process flow of Aadhaar seeding a. The student has to visit the bank branch where she is holding an account and submit the duly filled consent form b. question: Under the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), what is One-Time Registration (OTR)?
answer: One-Time Registration (OTR) is a unique number provided to streamline the scholarship registration process. Users register with their mobile number and complete e-KYC (electronic Know Your Customer). The OTR number is generated once and remains valid throughout the student's academic career.

question: Is there any evaluation process for continuation of ICAR NTS-PG Scholarship?
answer: The continuation of the ICAR NTS-PG scholarship is subject to good conduct, punctuality and minimum prescribed performance [OGPA/CGPA of minimum 7.00 OUT of 10.00 (6.50/10.00 for SC/ST)].

question: Who is eligible to get ICAR-Post Graduate Studies (PGS) Scholarship?
answer: There are limited slots for ICAR-Post Graduate Studies (PGS) Scholarship. 600 fellowships are awarded every year based on the merit obtained through All India Entrance Examination (AIEE).

question: Are students admitted in State Agricultural Universities through their entrance test eligible for ICAR-Post Graduate Studies (PGS) Scholarship?
answer: No. Students admitted through All India Entrance Examination (AIEE) in the Agricultural University under ICAR All India Quota (AIQ) seats in the Agricultural Universities under ICAR-AU System are only eligible.

question: Do I have to apply separately for ICAR-Post Graduate Studies (PGS) Scholarship?
answer: No. Candidates who appeared and admitted through All India Entrance Examination (AIEE) in the Agricultural University under ICAR AIQ Seats are automatically eligible for the said scholarship based on the set criteria.
